title: NEB Class 11 Physics — Reflection at Curved Mirror — 2024
subject: physics
topicTitle: NEB Class 11 Physics — Reflection at Curved Mirror — 2024
source: NEB Grade 11 Model Questions / NEB Past Papers 2020-2024

questions.question: Derive the mirror formula 1/v + 1/u = 1/f for a concave mirror, stating the sign convention used.
questions.solution:
Cartesian sign convention: distances measured in front of the mirror are negative; f of a concave mirror is negative.

From similar triangles in the ray diagram (object AB, image A′B′, centre of curvature C, focus F): AB/A′B′ = u/(u − R) = (u − f)/(v − f)... solving the geometry gives 1/v + 1/u = **2/R = 1/f**.

(With the older 'all distances positive' convention the same algebra yields 1/f = 1/v + 1/u.)
questions.knowledgeNote: Mirror formula and lens formula differ by a sign (1/v + 1/u = 1/f vs 1/v − 1/u = 1/f) — the commonest formula swap in NEB.

questions.question: Derive the relation f = R/2 for a spherical mirror.
questions.solution:
A ray parallel to the axis at small height h strikes a mirror of radius R. The normal at that point is the radius, making angle θ ≈ h/R with the axis.

By reflection the ray turns through 2θ and crosses the axis at F where h/F-distance... paraxial geometry gives the crossing at R/2 from the pole. Hence **f = R/2**.

(Valid only for paraxial rays — wide beams suffer spherical aberration.)
questions.knowledgeNote: f = R/2 is why a 30 cm radius mirror focuses parallel sunlight 15 cm in front of it.

questions.question: An object is placed 10 cm in front of a concave mirror of focal length 15 cm. Find the image position and magnification. State the image nature.
questions.solution:
Cartesian: f = −15 cm, u = −10 cm.

1/v = 1/f − 1/u = −1/15 + 1/10 = 1/30 → v = **+30 cm** (behind the mirror → virtual).

m = −v/u = −30/(−10) = **+3**: erect and 3× magnified.
questions.knowledgeNote: Object inside F always gives a virtual, erect, magnified image — the shaving-mirror case.

questions.question: Define linear magnification for a mirror and write its relation with image and object distances.
questions.solution:
**Linear magnification** m = height of image / height of object = h′/h.

From similar triangles, m = **−v/u** (Cartesian). |m| > 1 means enlarged; negative m means inverted (real image).
questions.knowledgeNote: m = −v/u for mirrors vs m = v/u for lenses — the minus is the tell-tale of reflection.

questions.question: Write two uses each of concave and convex mirrors.
questions.solution:
**Concave:** (1) shaving/make-up mirrors (erect magnified virtual image); (2) headlight and torch reflectors (parallel beam); (3) solar concentrators.

**Convex:** (1) vehicle rear-view mirrors (wide, erect, diminished field); (2) blind-corner and shop security mirrors.
questions.knowledgeNote: 'Always virtual, erect, diminished' is the convex-mirror fingerprint — an NEB one-mark gift.

questions.question: Why is a concave mirror used in a car headlight? Explain with a ray diagram description.
questions.solution:
The bulb is placed at the **focus** of the concave reflector. Rays from the focus strike the mirror and reflect **parallel to the principal axis** (reversibility of the parallel-to-focus ray).

The result is a powerful directed beam instead of light scattering in all directions.
questions.knowledgeNote: Searchlights and satellite dishes exploit the same focus ↔ parallel-beam reversibility.
